subject: Log governance: region-specific retention, export windows, and proof-of-deletion
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Leah Ford <leah.ford@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: audit/access log retention & exports (US residency)

Hi Stephanie,

Following up from our vendor assessment call — a couple of specific asks from our infosec team around audit and access logs before we sign the SOW:

1) What are the default retention windows for audit logs vs. access (login/change) logs for US-resident tenants? We need a clear number of days and any tiered defaults.
2) Can we request a one-time bulk export of the last 18 months of audit logs? Preferred formats are NDJSON or Parquet; we may need incremental exports.
3) For exports, can we choose customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM)? Also need to know transfer encryption and storage lifetime on Redwood side.
4) If we request account termination and data deletion, what evidence can you provide that audit/access logs were removed from Redwood systems (proof-of-deletion)? Is there a retention purge queue and how long until irrecoverable deletion?

We attached a short CSV with the fields our auditors expect. Appreciate short, concrete answers we can pass back to procurement.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of IT Security, Crestline Therapeutics
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Leah Ford <leah.ford@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: audit/access log retention & exports (US residency)

Evan — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I'll loop in Ben from Security for the low-level details:

- Default retention (US tenant): audit logs = 12 months (365 days); access/login events = 90 days. We offer extended retention add-ons (up to 7 years) for enterprise contracts.
- Bulk export: yes, one-time export of 18 months is possible. Supported formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), Parquet, and gzipped CSV. Incremental exports (monthly slices) are also supported for large windows.
- Encryption: exports can be encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3). At-rest on our export staging is AES-256; we support customer-managed KMS for the exported bundle when arranged in the contract.
- Deletion/proof: we provide a signed deletion certificate and export manifest (checksums) showing objects removed and purge timestamps. There's a 30-day irrevocable deletion queue after a deletion job starts for Shared & Hosted tenants; Dedicated/Private options can have shorter or configurable windows by contract.

I'll let Ben add the operational playbook and how we handle regioned shards and residual backups. If you want an official export quote (size + cost), tell us preferred format and whether you want a single bundle or incremental slices.

- Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: audit/access log retention & exports (US residency)

Evan / team — Ben from Security ops here. More detail and operational notes so your auditors can validate:

1) Retention mechanics and regional sharding
- Audit logs (control-plane events, API actions, config changes) are stored in a US region by default for US tenants. Physical shards are tagged with region metadata; retention is applied at shard level.
- Default TTLs are implemented as retention_policy = {"audit":365, "access":90} days in our metadata service. For enterprise customers we can set a custom TTL per-tenant which applies to both hot and cold stores.

2) Export flow and formats
- Export request steps: 1) request via Console/API -> 2) preflight (estimate size/objects) -> 3) prepare export bundle (NDJSON/Parquet/CSV) -> 4) encrypt and stage -> 5) provide signed download link or push to customer S3.
- NDJSON is the most straightforward for per-event ingestion; Parquet reduces size for analytic backfills. We recommend Parquet for >100GB exports.
- Incremental exports: we can stream monthly slices; each slice has independent manifest + checksum. That helps with resumability.

3) Keys, transport, and staging lifetime
- Transport = TLS 1.3.
- At-rest staging is AES-256. Customer-managed KMS: we support both AWS KMS (granting access to Redwood export IAM role) and external HSM via an enterprise connector; however, HSM integrations require a lead time to configure (typically 2–4 weeks).
- Staging lifetime: by default staged bundles are available for 7 days for download unless you select a pushed-to-customer-S3 delivery which removes them from Redwood staging immediately after successful push.

4) Deletion semantics and proof-of-deletion
- Deletion happens in two phases: a logical delete (immediate) and a physical purge cycle. For Hosted customers the physical purge runs on a 30-day cadence; during that window data is logically inaccessible. For Dedicated/Private, purge cadence can be contracted down to 7 days or immediate (for air-gapped installs).
- Proof we provide: signed deletion certificate (ISO8601 timestamps), object-level manifests with SHA256 checksums, and a log of purge jobs with job IDs you can reconcile. For additional assurance we can share redacted internal job run logs under NDA.

5) Backups and immutable snapshot considerations
- Long-term backups (snapshots) are kept for operational recovery; snapshots inherit tenant retention policies. Snapshots that fall within the retention TTL will also be rotated and purged according to the contracted policy. For customers requiring deletions from backups outside standard TTLs, we provide a custom remediation plan (usually part of Dedicated/Private contracts).

6) Cost and timing for an 18-month export
- Example estimate: 18 months of audit logs for a mid-sized tenant (~120GB compressed) — export prep and packaging: 24–48 hours; transfer time depends on delivery method (S3 push typically completes within the staging window). Export request fee applies (one-time) unless covered in the support package. I can run numbers if Evan shares approximate retention size or event rate.

If you want, I can attach an export playbook (sample job manifest) and a short checklist for your auditors.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Security Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: audit/access log retention & exports (US residency)

Evan — attaching the export field map and a small sample NDJSON file (see attachments). Two quick choices for you to confirm so we can issue an export PO:

A) Delivery format: Parquet (recommended if >100GB) or NDJSON (if you want event-by-event).
B) Delivery method: push to your S3 (requires AWS account + IAM role) OR signed download link (7-day staging).

If you want proof-of-deletion included in the export package, we add the deletion certificate as a separate signed artifact after the purge completes. If you need HSM/KMS-managed exports, let us know and Ben will open the onboarding ticket (2–4 week SLA).

Next step: Evan, can you confirm format + delivery method and whether Crestline will require customer-managed KMS? Then we'll create an export estimate and timeline.

Thanks — Steph
